proposedEntry.name: dashboard-design
proposedEntry.description: Runs a structured requirements -> layout -> visualization workflow for dashboard design (Vizro-flavored but largely tool-agnostic): Step 1 gathers users/goals/data/structure and applies the 7±2 KPI rule with a 3-level information hierarchy; Step 2 defines navigation, filter placement and ASCII wireframes; Step 3 selects chart types and enforces no-custom-KPI-card rules. Each step produces a spec file for resumable, reviewable design decisions, and a common_mistakes.md anti-pattern library covers all three steps (information overload, poor hierarchy, wrong chart types, color misuse, missing context).
inputs: end users, decisions, and data sources for the dashboard
approved wireframes and chart/KPI choices at each step gate
outputs: spec/1_information_architecture.md, spec/2_interaction_ux.md, spec/3_visual_design.md documenting requirements, layout/wireframes, and chart selections

#### mckinsey/vizro (inspected 2026-08-29)
- Repo pin: a12d760aa45233d68f4ef3f1cec9cc8b5fcda48f (default branch main), 3,785 stars, pushed 2026-08-28T23:03:54Z. Root license file is LICENSE.txt (LICENSE and LICENSE.md both 404): Apache License 2.0, full text read.
- vizro-e2e-flow/skills/ contains 6 skills forming one chained Vizro workflow: dashboard-build, dashboard-design, designing-vizro-layouts, selecting-vizro-charts, wiring-vizro-actions, writing-vizro-yaml.
- Read SKILL.md and all 6 bundled files (3 spec-template assets, 3 references) in full.
- Task-specific check: how much of dashboard-design stands on its own vs. is a pure Vizro API manual. Step 1 (Understand Requirements) is fully general and well-developed -- 7±2 KPI rule, user-archetype table, analytical-question framing, page-structure patterns, all reusable outside Vizro. references/wireframe_templates.md (ASCII wireframe conventions) and references/common_mistakes.md's Step 1 and Step 3 sections are also largely general dashboard-design wisdom. BUT: Step 2 (layout & interaction), which the SKILL.md itself frames as a required, non-skippable stage, explicitly delegates its actual content -- grid system, component sizing, filter-placement rules ('Load the designing-vizro-layouts skill') and all interaction-pattern definitions (the 6 named Patterns 1-6, referenced by name throughout common_mistakes.md and wireframe_templates.md but never defined in any file in this skill's own directory) -- to two sibling skill directories (vizro-e2e-flow/skills/designing-vizro-layouts, vizro-e2e-flow/skills/wiring-vizro-actions) that live outside dashboard-design/. Step 3's chart-type-selection and color-strategy specifics are likewise deferred to vizro-e2e-flow/skills/selecting-vizro-charts. An agent given only the dashboard-design directory cannot complete roughly half of its own mandated 3-step workflow, and cannot resolve the Pattern 1-6 references it uses.
- Self-containment rule applied: bundling the three sibling skills was considered and rejected -- they are Vizro-API-specific (Vizro's own grid/action/chart components), so pulling them in would mean vendoring Vizro-API-manual content under a 'product design' skill id, contrary to the task's explicit instruction to reject content that is 'purely a Vizro API manual'. The clean alternative is the one the rule offers: keep the skill, name the external dependency, don't vendor.
- Rubric computed as if vendored (for record): relevance 3, quality 2 (Step 1 and the wireframe/mistakes content are strong, but the workflow's own Step 2/3 core guidance is not actually present in the vendorable files), conformance 1 (unresolvable cross-skill references for a mandated workflow step), uniqueness 2. Total 8 -- would ordinarily clear the vendor bar, but the self-containment rule overrides.
- Security: clean.
- Verdict: not-vendored-keeper.
